# Full Spec Coverage Checklist: AI Workout Tracker

**Purpose**: Standard-depth, author-facing pre-`/speckit-tasks` review of spec.md requirements quality across all categories — completeness, clarity, consistency, measurability, and scenario/edge-case coverage.
**Created**: 2026-08-31
**Feature**: [spec.md](../spec.md)

**Note**: This custom checklist is generated by the `/speckit-checklist` command based on feature context and requirements.
**Review Ownership**: This checklist is a reviewer-owned requirements-quality review artifact. Mark an item `[x]` only when the reviewer determines the requirements-quality criterion is satisfied.
**Marker Semantics**: `[x]` means the criterion has been reviewed and satisfied for requirements quality. It does not mean implementation work is complete.

## Requirement Completeness

- [ ] CHK001 Are requirements defined for how the fatigue/recovery signal is computed (inputs, weighting, thresholds) beyond "recent volume, intensity, frequency, and recency"? [Completeness, Spec §FR-005]
- [ ] CHK002 Is the exercise-catalog fuzzy-match/dedupe behavior specified anywhere beyond "the system MUST add it"? [Gap, Spec §FR-021]
- [ ] CHK003 Are requirements defined for what qualifies as a "minor edit" in SC-002, versus an edit large enough to no longer count? [Completeness, Spec §SC-002]
- [ ] CHK004 Are requirements defined for the actual cap value / reset cadence behind FR-022's "soft daily cap," or only its existence? [Gap, Spec §FR-022]
- [ ] CHK005 Are requirements defined for what happens to an in-progress AI chat conversation if the user navigates away before accepting or rejecting a proposal? [Gap, Spec §US1]
- [ ] CHK006 Are requirements defined for removing a previously recorded preference entry entirely (not just adding/updating goals, equipment, or injuries)? [Completeness, Spec §FR-016]

## Requirement Clarity

- [ ] CHK007 Is "a reasonable workout" (no prior history case) bounded clearly enough that two reviewers would agree on pass/fail? [Clarity, Spec §US1 Acceptance Scenario 2]
- [ ] CHK008 Is "minor edits" in SC-002 defined precisely enough to be measured consistently across reviewers? [Clarity, Spec §SC-002]
- [ ] CHK009 Is "soft daily cap" in FR-022 clarified with a concrete numeric threshold, or left fully open to implementation choice? [Ambiguity, Spec §FR-022]
- [ ] CHK010 Is "clear error message" (FR-020) specified with required content (e.g., cause, next step), or left to interpretation? [Clarity, Spec §FR-020]
- [ ] CHK011 Is "materially change the resulting workout" (FR-004) defined with a bounded set of triggering conditions, or only illustrated by example? [Clarity, Spec §FR-004]

## Requirement Consistency

- [ ] CHK012 Are the "any workout" editability guarantees in FR-007–FR-009 stated consistently with FR-009a's explicit no-read-only-state clause, without one implying a narrower scope than the other? [Consistency, Spec §FR-007-FR-009a]
- [ ] CHK013 Is "previously loaded workouts" (FR-017) defined consistently with SC-005's "100% of previously loaded workout data," so both refer to the same trigger for what counts as "loaded"? [Consistency, Spec §FR-017/SC-005]
- [ ] CHK014 Are the AI-failure behaviors described in FR-020 and in the matching Edge Cases entry worded consistently, with no divergent implied behavior? [Consistency, Spec §FR-020/Edge Cases]
- [ ] CHK015 Do FR-022 (default-access cap) and FR-023 (custom-key bypass) agree on exactly which requests are counted vs. exempted, leaving no request type unaccounted for? [Consistency, Spec §FR-022-FR-023]

## Acceptance Criteria Quality

- [ ] CHK016 Can SC-002's "90% of AI-generated workouts require no more than minor edits" be objectively measured without a defined sampling method or observation window? [Measurability, Spec §SC-002]
- [ ] CHK017 Can SC-006's "95% of first-time users successfully complete and save a logged workout without external help" be verified without a defined test cohort/protocol? [Measurability, Spec §SC-006]
- [ ] CHK018 Can SC-007's "measurably shift toward lower intensity" be verified given no logging/audit requirement exists elsewhere in the spec to capture suggestion history over time? [Measurability, Spec §SC-007]
- [ ] CHK019 Do the User Story 4 acceptance scenarios provide enough observable behavior to verify FR-016's "system MUST use the current values in subsequent AI suggestions"? [Acceptance Criteria, Spec §US4/FR-016]

## Scenario Coverage

- [ ] CHK020 Are requirements defined for the primary flow of manually creating a workout end-to-end, including where/how workout type is chosen? [Coverage, Gap, Spec §FR-015]
- [ ] CHK021 Are alternate-flow requirements defined for a user rejecting or discarding an AI-proposed workout without accepting it? [Coverage, Gap, Spec §US1]
- [ ] CHK022 Are exception-flow requirements defined for a user noticing and correcting an unwanted duplicate created by the exercise-catalog matching behavior? [Coverage, Gap, Spec §FR-021]
- [ ] CHK023 Are recovery-flow requirements defined for resuming an in-progress timed workout after the app is fully closed and later reopened (as distinct from a brief backgrounding)? [Coverage, Gap, Spec §FR-012]
- [ ] CHK024 Are requirements defined for the single local profile being open in two tabs/devices at the same time? [Coverage, Gap, Spec §FR-018]

## Edge Case Coverage

- [ ] CHK025 Is the interaction between the documented "empty workout" edge case and the AI-usage-cap edge case checked for conflicts (e.g., can an empty workout still be "accepted" while capped)? [Consistency, Spec §Edge Cases]
- [ ] CHK026 Are requirements defined for an invalid or revoked custom API key (FR-023) — does the system fall back to the default cap, block outright, or something else? [Gap, Spec §FR-023]
- [ ] CHK027 Are requirements defined for an ambiguous catalog match between two similarly named existing exercises (as opposed to new-vs-existing)? [Gap, Spec §FR-021]
- [ ] CHK028 Are requirements defined for out-of-range entry values (e.g., negative reps/weight, zero-second interval) entered during editing? [Gap, Spec §FR-008]

## Non-Functional Requirements

- [ ] CHK029 Are accessibility requirements specified for the AI chat and workout-execution UI? [Gap, Non-Functional]
- [ ] CHK030 Are localization requirements beyond the kg/lb unit preference addressed (e.g., date formats, language of AI responses)? [Gap, Spec §Assumptions]
- [ ] CHK031 Are data-retention or deletion requirements specified for logged workouts, chat history, or a removed custom API key? [Gap, Non-Functional]
- [ ] CHK032 Is FR-017's offline requirement paired with any storage-limit or cache-size expectation, or left fully open-ended? [Completeness, Spec §FR-017]

## Dependencies & Assumptions

- [ ] CHK033 Is the assumption that "the AI chat requires network connectivity" reconciled with any requirement for degraded-but-present connectivity (slow, not absent)? [Assumption, Spec §Assumptions]
- [ ] CHK034 Is the dependency on external AI-provider availability/response time reflected in any requirement beyond the failure-message behavior in FR-020? [Dependency, Gap]
- [ ] CHK035 Is the Assumptions-section scope of "previously logged workout history" (this app only, not imported) consistently reflected everywhere FR-002 and FR-005 reference workout history? [Consistency, Spec §Assumptions/FR-002/FR-005]

## Ambiguities & Conflicts

- [ ] CHK036 Is there a requirement stating who or what triggers a workout's draft/in-progress/completed status transition, or is this left undefined? [Ambiguity, Spec §Key Entities]
- [ ] CHK037 Is "a typical request" in SC-001's 3-minute target bounded so that request complexity can't make the criterion untestable? [Ambiguity, Spec §SC-001]

## Notes

- Mark items `[x]` only after review confirms the requirement-quality criterion is satisfied
- Leave items unchecked when they still require clarification, correction, or reviewer evaluation
- `/speckit-implement` reads checklist checkbox state as a gate and must not modify markers
- `checklists/requirements.md` has a separate built-in lifecycle maintained by `/speckit-specify` and `/speckit-clarify`
- Add comments or findings inline
- Link to relevant resources or documentation
- Items are numbered sequentially for easy reference
